Item: General
Website or individual pages are not down or timing out.
Where To Check: Automated tools like Pingdom, Screaming Frog Crawl, Ahrefs, or manual testing.
Notes/Reference:
If you run a tool and it reports a timeout, check the page in your browser. If it's not timing out for you, then you may need to whitelist the tool's IP addresses with your host (you can usually find IP ranges on the tool's website). 
If the issue does persist in a browser, you may need technical support with your server from your host.

Item: Sitemap doesn't contain functioning URLs that you want to keep out of the index.

Item: Pages returning 404 status codes redirect to relevant pages if applicable.
Notes/Reference: When pages move, you often end up with 404 errors. Redirect to relevant pages if they exist. Google's documentation on 404s says that 404s aren't inherently problematic, but you want to make sure you're not serving errors when you should be serving content.

Item: Pages that you wish to remove from the index serve 410 HTTP status code.
Notes/Reference: Technically, Google treats 404s and 410s the same way, and you should see them disappear after a while. Do not block 404s in your robots.txt.

Item: Internal links resolve 200 OK.
Notes/Reference: How To Find And Fix Broken Links

Item: The site has no redirect chains.
Notes/Reference: Redirect chains don't technically hurt you, but aim for less than five redirects, per Google's John Mueller.

Item: Site does not use JavaScript redirection. (For headless sites, implement carefully.)
Notes/Reference: This is a bit of a grey area. Google strongly prefers traditional server-side redirects and advises against JavaScript redirects. However, you can use them for some situations, like headless architecture, if you go about it carefully.

Item: Site does not use HTML meta refresh tags.
Notes/Reference: Google doesn't recommend using meta refresh tags as they can be confusing, and are not supported by all browsers.
